title: Local Inference Engines on Apple Silicon: MLX-LM, Ollama, llama.cpp and the InferenceEngine Abstraction
content: Three production-ready options serve local LLMs on Apple Silicon in 2026: MLX-LM (Apple's Metal-native Python framework, pip-installable, exposes mlx_lm.generate for in-process calls and mlx_lm.server for an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint on 127.0.0.1:8080), Ollama (a daemon wrapping llama.cpp — or MLX since v0.19 on 32 GB+ Macs — exposing OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions at port 11434, with built-in tool-calling for Qwen3, Llama 3.x, and Mistral families), and llama.cpp / llama-server directly (GGUF quantised models, Metal via -ngl 999, grammar-constrained JSON output via --jinja and grammar files, lowest-level control). MLX leads by 20-87 % on models under 14 B parameters (compute-bound); above 27 B the engines converge on memory bandwidth; Ollama v0.19+ adopted MLX as its Apple Silicon backend so the performance gap between the two largely closed for 32 GB+ machines. For an agentic operator loop, the cleanest architecture defines a narrow InferenceEngine Protocol (chat method returning a typed response), ships a deterministic OfflineStub for CI, and mounts either an MlxLmAdapter (hitting mlx_lm.server) or an OllamaAdapter (hitting Ollama's /v1 endpoint) at runtime — the agent loop never imports the model library directly. Temperature=0 enforces greedy decoding (deterministic token selection) but does not guarantee bit-exact reproduction across runs because of floating-point batching effects; the practical answer is structured JSON output via response_format={type:json_object} or Pydantic schema-constrained tool calls, so the agent loop validates the shape at the system boundary rather than relying on probabilistic repeatability.
lesson: The ark operator loop (state -> action -> feedback -> revision) must be testable without a running model, so the InferenceEngine abstraction is load-bearing: the OfflineStub lets CI run the full loop deterministically, while the MlxLmAdapter or OllamaAdapter hot-swaps in at runtime with zero changes to the loop body. The LLM's role in ark is strictly to propose (choose a strategy variant, diagnose a failure, emit a tool call) while numpy and MLX execute — keeping the model off the numeric hot path preserves the measured performance guarantees of the kernel layer.
key_usages: drive the operator agentic loop (engineer/test/repair/audit strategies) fully offline in CI via OfflineStub
swap to mlx_lm.server or Ollama /v1 at runtime without modifying any loop logic
emit structured JSON tool calls for strategy mutation, regime classification, and audit diagnostics
gate model output at the system boundary with Pydantic schema validation before handing results to numpy/MLX execution

key_codes.code:
# terminal: mlx_lm.server --model mlx-community/Qwen3-8B-4bit --port 8080

from openai import OpenAI

class MlxLmAdapter:
    def __init__(self, model='mlx-community/Qwen3-8B-4bit', port=8080):
        self.client = OpenAI(base_url=f'http://127.0.0.1:{port}/v1', api_key='local')
        self.model = model
    def chat(self, messages, tools=None, **kw):
        resp = self.client.chat.completions.create(
            model=self.model, messages=messages,
            tools=tools, temperature=0,
            response_format={'type': 'json_object'} if not tools else None,
            **kw)
        m = resp.choices[0].message
        return ChatResponse(content=m.content or '', tool_calls=[tc.model_dump() for tc in (m.tool_calls or [])])
